scenario.title: A teammate is about to walk away
scenario.situation: Your team of four is building an app for a city hackathon, and the demo is in three days. Dana wrote most of the backend. Last night Timur rewrote her module without asking, and this morning she says she is out.
scenario.goal: Get to the demo without losing anyone. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Dana
character.wants: To be asked before her work is changed

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Honestly, I'm done. Timur rewrote my whole module last night without a word to me. If my work can just be thrown away, why am I even here? Maybe the three of you can finish the demo without me.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Okay, let's fix this fast. The demo is in three days, so we can't lose you now. Send me the list of what Timur changed and I'll look at it tonight.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Okay… I hear you. But it isn't only about the code. Nobody asked me anything. How do I know it won't happen again next week?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: From now on nobody merges into someone else's module without a review from its owner. I'll set that rule in the repo today.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Fine, I could talk to him. But the demo is in three days and his version still breaks the login. Who decides which version we keep?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We keep your version for the demo because it works. Timur moves his changes to a separate branch and we look at them after Thursday. If his login fix is really needed, the risk is that we demo with a known bug, so I'll ask him to patch only that.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: That sounds fair, I guess. So what do I actually do today? I don't want to sit around waiting for Timur to agree with me.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Today you finish the payment endpoint, Timur fixes the login in his branch, and I write the demo script. We freeze the backend by Thursday noon and do a full run at six.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Alright. If we write down who owns what, I'm in. But you tell Timur, not me. I don't want another argument tonight.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Deal. I'll put the owners in the team chat in ten minutes and call Timur right after. If the Thursday run fails, we cut the analytics screen instead of working all night.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Okay. Let's try it your way. And thanks for actually listening.
